assistant_question: Order135 is the final cross-rules audit. It can’t certify full closure while Order134’s in-turn deployment prerequisite remains open. I recommend completing the full audit and reporting that gap explicitly. Shall I proceed on that basis?
user_answer: The concept of "in-turn deployment" is not a core role, otherwise we would be aware of it. It might be a faction ability/rule, which is fine therefore how we scoped Order134 allowing for that. Given that, I don't think the "core rule" audit should remain open as it's not a core rule. There will be other rules that factions bring that are exceptions to core rules anyways that will need to be supported.
current_acceptance_effect: Absence of an admitted in-turn deployment granting ability is not a Core audit blocker. Assess Order134 conditional restrictions and existing real consumers, persistence and replay. A future source-admitted faction or mission granting rule is a separate capability and integration obligation. Full Core closure remains contingent on all actual Core obligations, required gates and both exact-final reviews.
historical_evidence: Order134 handoff, qualification and initial Order135 reports remain immutable issue-time evidence. This clarification supersedes the inference that absent granting permission itself prevents Core closure.
